story_type: Black Hawk water drops on a wildfire, spinning smoke column beside the helicopter
hook: A tower of spinning smoke, and a Black Hawk flying right past it.
narration: A spinning tower of smoke rose off a Nevada wildfire, and a Black Hawk flew right past it.
A day earlier, the Nevada Guard crew dipped its bucket into Pyramid Lake.
The bucket fills in seconds, then a valve opens it over the flames.
The next day they flew the Bug Fire near Stead, with flames racing through the brush.
Each drop cools hot spots and slows the fire for the crews on the ground.
outcome: The Nevada Guard Black Hawk crews hit the Bug Fire with water from the air.
title: Black Hawk vs a Nevada wildfire
description:
Nevada National Guard Black Hawk crews lift water from Pyramid Lake and drop it on wildfires near Reno-Stead, Nevada, in August 2026.

Footage: Nevada National Guard video by Staff Sgt. Zandra Duran, Nevada Joint Force Headquarters Public Affairs, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/1018490/firefighting-bucket-drop-nevada-national-guard

facts.claim: Nevada National Guard crews conduct aerial bucket drops on wildfires
facts.source_quote: The Nevada National Guard aviation pilots and crews are supporting firefighting operations for current wildfires by conducting aerial bucket drops to deliver water where they can make the fastest impact.

facts.claim: Drops cool hot spots, reduce intensity and support ground crews
facts.source_quote: These drops help cool hot spots, reduce fire intensity, and bolster ground efforts, giving incident teams a crucial tool to slow the spread of fire
